security_risks.concern: Household identity and player permissions lack an enforceable access matrix; an identifier change could expose another child
“Short-lived authorization” does not define revocation or leaked-link behavior
App-private files alone do not specify device confidentiality
Parent controls are mainly UX; a child-mode toggle could be mistaken for authorization
Consent withdrawal, family changes, and adulthood need a consistent state model
Deletion scope and stale uploads can conflict
A database backup could be mistaken for a recording backup
Video quotas and media processing lack abuse controls
Environment and secret boundaries are not detailed
Agent-readable issues and dependencies can carry hostile instructions
Retried events and lost workers can duplicate writes or charges
An agent can report success without accepted evidence
Supply-chain and Dart security coverage are unspecified
Content accuracy and rights are not yet approved
Operations, incident ownership, and recovery are incomplete
Commercial payments and release permissions require implementation evidence
Market, child audience, vendor scope, and data notices remain assumptions
Club and household relationships widen the isolation boundary; global roles or unsafe joins could expose unrelated users
Coach editing can change age suitability, prescriptions or published history
Club invitation, coach departure and family transfer could incorrectly grant guardianship or retain access
New administrative portal and exports create privileged attack paths
Club-funded access or assigned practice could silently expose personal recordings and unrelated activity
Local accounts, schema migration or queued events expose/corrupt another player's data or restore deleted data
Forged, duplicated, delayed or misbound billing events grant features or charge the wrong household
Store payment route, age audience or third-party SDK practices contradict the actual child experience
Primary-region failure or deletion leaves orphaned footage or unusable recovery; residency claims exceed reality
Quota, billing, support or operational failures harm families or leave incidents unowned
